name: MedAlign
intro: MedAlign是由临床医生生成的电子病历指令遵循评测数据集，包含983条临床指令和303条人工参考回复，旨在评估大型语言模型在真实医疗场景中的指令遵循和EHR处理能力。
build_method: 临床医生指令收集、BM25病历匹配、专家参考回复
metric: 临床正确率, 胜率, 平均排名, Kendall Tau
task_type: 指令遵循, 文本生成
eval_feature: 三阶段策展, 盲法临床评审, 自动NLG指标相关性
scale: 983条指令, 303条人工参考回复, 276份电子病历
build_method_en: Clinician instruction collection, BM25 EHR matching, expert reference responses
eval_feature_en: Three-stage curation, blinded clinician review, automated NLG-metric correlation
intro_en: MedAlign is an electronic health record instruction-following evaluation dataset generated by clinicians, containing 983 clinical instructions and 303 human reference responses. It aims to assess large language models' instruction-following and EHR processing capabilities in real medical scenarios.

drawio_review_note: Reviewed against arXiv:2308.14089v2 (revised 2023-12-24), official repository commit 4a88e4744ea31b1fdea8b191fdc9e4dc05cf624e, and the credentialed Redivis dataset record 48nr-frxd97exb. The paper contract recruits 15 clinicians across seven specialties by email and online form; collects 1,314 instructions with patient characteristics and clinical context; removes near duplicates at ROUGE-L > 0.7 to retain 983, of which 407 are generally applicable; builds instruction-plus-metadata queries; indexes timestamped structured and free-text OMOP events as one XML record each over a random 77,200-patient hospital subsample; retrieves BM25 top five from the same pool used by the random baseline; and reviews candidates in rank order until the first relevant EHR. This yields 240/407 rank-one matches (59%), 303/407 top-five matches (74%), versus 38% random; unmatched instructions remain in the 983-item catalog but leave the grounded-response subset. Same-specialty non-authors are preferred for response writing, with feasibility, EHR-sufficiency and latest-timestamp checks; the paper reports 303 references for 303 pairs across 276 distinct EHRs but does not quantify response-stage failures. Six configurations reserve 256 generation tokens; direct prompts truncate the record beginning to retain recent context, while GPT-4 32k multi-step refinement processes 30k-token chunks from earliest to latest. Nine blinded clinicians view the full untruncated EHR, cannot review their own instruction or response, may tie ranks, and triple-review 50 pairs. Binary correctness uses clinical appropriateness, meaning preservation and instruction coverage; the main denominator is 303 pairs per configuration. Forty-four questions fail for one or more GPT-4 variants: the initial correctness analysis counts failed outputs incorrect, while supplemental analyses exclude the affected questions and use 259 pairs. The paper's main table reports rank over 303 pairs but does not disclose how content-filter errors or error messages were handled in rank assignment. Reports include correctness, mean rank, strict pairwise win rates, automated NLG metrics and mean Kendall tau against human ranks. Full data access requires Redivis approval, CITI training, a DUA and encrypted handling; redistribution and non-HIPAA commercial API use are prohibited. Version drift is explicit: paper v2 says 276 distinct EHRs, while the pinned public repository says 275, with no reconciliation. The repository exposes samples but no evaluator; free-text outputs have no answer parser, and official metric-code versions are not released there. Formal publication evidence [site-a11s-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2136×1501 (English) and 2125×1501 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2134×1499 and 2123×1499. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
